title: Starting in television and recording with Stanley Wilson
summary: Stanley Wilson asked him to score M Squad segments, his introduction to TV and to full composition and underscoring.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Not the TV show.
Well, was there a film, "M Squad"?
I think there was.
Well, maybe. I don't know. Either that,
or was it a segment of 'M Squad' or a segment of something else.
That was on TV ... there was a TV show called 'M Squad'.
If it was 'M Squad', now I'm not sure.
Oh, I'm sorry.
But it was a segment of something.
Right.

And Herman had done it as a composer and Stanley Wilson was the music head, and after we finished doing this, and I had met Stanley. he asked me if I'd be interested in doing composition on 'M Squad,' you know ... doing a segment.
This is the TV show.
The TV? Well, was there a picture called 'M Squad?'
I don't know.
I don't think so.
I don't think so. Stanley Wilson, at that time, asked you in his capacity as head of music for Universal?
That's right.
I see.
Yes. And if I would be interested in, you know, doing an 'M Squad' segment. And I said yes. So I did one, after which they asked me if I would like to do another ... finish the series.
Uh huh. So that was your
introduction to TV?

To TV and to composition. Because prior to that, I'd only done arranging and orchestrating. And then with doing TV, which meant that I had to do all of the background, you know, the underscoring of everything that was done. In essence, when I started doing it, then it was my picture, my responsibility completely.
Right. And that was the beginning of that phase of your Hollywood career?
That's right.
Uh huh. And then you had a lot to do with Stanley Wilson in his capacity as Universal head; music, both in films and in TV.
Well, actually, I never did a film at Universal.
Oh, I see.
Not a full film ... not a theatrical film.
Oh, I see.
I'd done one project, [Four and Twenty] (PHONETIC) which is like ... that's a two hour show, but it's still for TV, and that differs in category from a theatrical film.
Right. And then you did some records with -- some recording, I think, with Stanley Wilson.
Yes ... yes.
Right.
How long ago did he die?
It seems he died in 1970, I believe.
